column1: # boru Language Specification: the var word
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `var NAME value` / `var NAME:Type value` (design/IMMUTABLE-DEF.1.md §2.3):
# the one binding whose value changes in place. A var visible within the
# current frame is ASSIGNED; otherwise one is DECLARED in the current scope.
# A var of another frame is readable, never assignable. A var holds a value,
# never a function constructor or a type. Rows run on both lanes.
# §1  declare and assign
var n 0 n
column3: a declaration binds the value

column1: var n 0 var n 5 n
column3: an assignment replaces it

column1: var n 0 var n 5 var n 6 n
column3: assignments repeat

column1: var s "a" var s "b" s
column3: a string var

column1: var xs [1 2] var xs (push 3 xs) xs
column3: a list var reassigned from its own value

column1: var m {a:1} var m (m set b/q 2) m
column3: a map var

column1: # §2  loop state — the counter and accumulator idioms
var n 0 for 3 [var n (n add 1)] n
column3: the loop counter

column1: var t 0 for 5 [var t (t add i)] t
column3: the accumulator over the index

column1: var n 0 while [n lt 3] [var n (n add 1)] n
column3: a while counter

column1: var n 0 var m 10 while [n lt 3] [var n (n add 1) var m (m sub 1)] [n m]
column3: two vars carried by one loop

column1: var t 0 each [var t (t add 1) t] [1 2 3]
column3: an each body assigns the enclosing var and yields it

column1: var t 0 each [var t (t add 1) t] [1 2 3] t
column3: the var holds the last assignment after the each

column1: var acc [] each [var acc (push 1 acc)] [7 8] acc
column3: an accumulator through each (the each yields its elements, the body having left nothing)

column1: var n 0 while [n lt 3] [if (n eq 1) [var n 5] [var n (n add 1)]] n
column3: an assignment inside a branch inside a loop

column1: var n 0 if true [var n 1] [var n 2] n
column3: a branch arm assigns

column1: def c (1 lt 2) var n 0 if c [var n 1] [var n 2] n
column3: a branch arm assigns under a computed condition

column1: var n 0 do [var n 4] n
column3: do is transparent: the body assigns the enclosing var

column1: # §3  frames — a fn body's own vars, a module var read but not assigned
def f fn [[] [Integer] [var n 0 var n (n add 1) n]] (f)
column3: a fn-local var

column1: def f fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [var n 0 for k [var n (n add i)] n]] f 4
column3: a fn-local var carried by a loop

column1: def f fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [var n 0 while [n lt k] [var n (n add 1)] n]] f 4
column3: a fn-local var carried by a while

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [Integer] [var s 0 def _ (each [var s (s add 1)] xs) s]] f [1 2 3]
column3: a fn-local var assigned by an each body (the each's own result bound aside)

column1: def g fn [[c:Boolean] [Integer] [var n 0 if c [var n 1] [var n 2] n]] g true
column3: a fn-local var assigned by a branch arm

column1: var n 0 def peek fn [[] [Integer] [n]] var n 5 (peek)
column3: a module var is read live by a fn body

column1: var n 0 def inc fn [[] [Integer] [var n (n add 1)]] (inc)
column3: a fn body cannot assign a module var

column1: var n 0 def inc fn [[] [Integer] [var n 7 n]] (inc)
column3: nor assign it a fresh value: the module's n is visible, so this is an assignment

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [var n 1 def g ([] => [n]) var n 2 (g)]] (f)
column3: a closure captures the var's value at creation

column1: var n 0 def mk fn [[] [Function] [([] => [n])]] def g (mk) var n 7 (g)
column3: a module var read by a closure stays live (the module is no frame of the closure)

column1: var acc [] each ([x] => [var acc (push x acc)]) [1 2]
column3: a lambda is a frame: it cannot assign the enclosing var

column1: each ([x] => [var y x y]) [1 2]
column3: a var declared inside a lambda is the lambda's own

column1: # §4  typed vars — the typed-name form (`var n:Integer 1`) is registered when
# the `var [[…]]` construct is deleted (basic/go/native_var.go's registration
# note); until then these rows are a comment, and VarTypedHandler is pinned
# by basic/go/native_var_test.go.
# var n:Integer 1 var n 2 n
column3: a typed var assigned a conforming value

column1: # var s:String "a" var s "b" s
column3: a typed string var

column1: # var n:Integer 1 var n "x"
column3: an assignment checks the declared type

column1: # var s:String 1
column3: the declaration checks it too

column1: # var x 1 var x:Integer 2
column3: a typed re-declaration of a live var is refused

column1: # def Pos refine Integer var p:Pos 3 var p 4 p
column3: a user type names a var's type

column1: # §5  a var holds a value
var T 1
column3: a capitalised name is a type

column1: var t Integer
column3: a type literal is no var value

column1: var f fn [[] [Integer] [1]]
column3: the fn constructor form is refused

column1: var C class {a:Integer}
column3: the class constructor form is refused

column1: var f ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) f 2
column3: a function VALUE computed at run time is stored and dispatches when read

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer] [Function] [([x:Integer] => [x add k])]] var f (mk 10) f 2
column3: a fn value from a factory likewise

column1: var add 1
column3: a core word's name is reserved

column1: # §6  var and def side by side (phase 3 makes a same-scope collision redefinition)
var x 1 def x 2 x
column3: today a def over a var shadows it

column1: def x 1 var x 2 x
column3: today a var over a def declares over it

column1: # §7  export — a module exports no var
import module [var n 5 export "M" {n: n}] M.n
column3: exporting a var is refused

column1: import module [var n 5 def m n export "M" {m: m}] M.m
column3: its value under a def exports
